clue.text: Instigate frolic in gym

indicators.note: the word for a frolic sits inside the letters for gym

parts.note: PT, physical training, is the school name for gym lessons
a romp is a boisterous frolic

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a bit of horseplay during a gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt something is to provoke or set it going.

clue.text: Fair father's fur

parts.note: PA is a familiar word for father, with the possessive S kept
sable is the prized fur of a small Asian marten

explanation.surface: A remark about the quality of a father's fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of middling or adequate: acceptable but not outstanding.

clue.text: No hunter discovered fugitive

indicators.note: read as dis-covered, the letters are exposed and jumbled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An escaped prisoner whom no pursuer has managed to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' looks like 'found', but it signals that the letters of NO HUNTER are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone escaping from the law is said to be fleeing, constantly moving to evade capture.

clue.text: Very cold fairy building at the bottom of the garden?

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology

parts.words: building at the bottom of the garden?
parts.note: a shed is the typical outbuilding at the end of a garden

explanation.surface: A frozen fairy lives in a little house at the end of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The fairies at the bottom of the garden are a nursery cliché; here the building there is just a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Perished is informal British speech for chilled through, frozen to the bone.

clue.text: Injury caused by spring in lock

indicators.note: the spring sits inside the lock of hair

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Damage done when a spring snaps inside a door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair; 'spring' is a water source, not a coil.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and older English a trespass is a wrongful act, a wrong done to someone.

clue.text: Make a comeback and do the twist again?

explanation.surface: An ageing dancer revives a career and the old rock-and-roll moves.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as RE-TURN: turn (twist) once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming back is to come home or reappear; read as re-turn it is to rotate a second time.

clue.text: Scene composed by a Roman dramatist

indicators.note: the letters are put together, made up anew, in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Roman playwright writes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges only the first word; the A is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger wrote tragedies in first-century Rome as well as philosophy.

clue.text: Well acquainted with gold if at exchange

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the letters are swapped round, exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who knows all about trading gold at the bullion exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English for being fully informed about or familiar with a subject.

clue.text: Setter being cryptic, in a way

indicators.note: a cryptic version of the word is one with its letters disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is being obscure, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as 'so to speak', but 'way' alone is the definition and 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A road with buildings along it is a common sort of way or thoroughfare.

clue.text: Planet or star unmoving?

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, split off the front of 'unmoving'

explanation.surface: Is that a planet or a fixed star in the night sky?
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmoving' looks like a description of a fixed star, but it splits in two: its front half joins the fodder and 'moving' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth planet from the sun, famous for its rings.

clue.text: Put up with champion

explanation.surface: Accepting something and defending a cause in one breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something; also to support or represent a cause or principle.

clue.text: A tantaliser resting

parts.note: a tease is someone who tantalises, leading people on

explanation.surface: A flirt lounging around at leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for relaxed and off duty, as in the military command to stand relaxed.

clue.text: Do race tips change for the better?

indicators.note: the letters alter their order, changing into another word

explanation.surface: A punter wonders whether tipsters' advice on races ever improves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the better?' hints at the purpose of the action: one does this repeatedly in order to improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something regularly to improve one's skill at it, as in rehearsing.

clue.text: Animal found in Arctic or Antarctic?

definitions.text: Animal found in Arctic or Antarctic?

parts.words: Animal found in Arctic or Antarctic?
parts.note: a playful reading: a feline living at either end of the earth's axis, which names a real European mammal

explanation.surface: A zoology question about creatures of the polar regions.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is not polar at all: it is a European weasel-like mammal whose name splits as a cat of the pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-furred mammal of the weasel family, known for its strong smell.

clue.text: Scan scam

explanation.surface: Two near-rhyming words for checking and cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: To pore over or study closely (an old sense); also a swindle or confidence trick.

clue.text: A river between lakes and bay

indicators.note: the letters for the lakes are set either side of the rest

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river runs between lakes and out into a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a coastal inlet beside the lakes, but it is the bay tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is the sweet laurel, whose leaves crowned victors.

clue.text: General wheels within wheels

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn round, so the letters run the other way
the letters wanted lie inside the second word

explanation.surface: The phrase for wheels within wheels, a complex hidden machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'wheels' is a reversal signal and 'within' a hiding signal: EEL lies in the second 'wheels' and turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army in the American Civil War.

clue.text: Prescribed plant

explanation.surface: Two words, perhaps for a doctor's orders and a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid down or fixed, as a set text; also a young plant or bulb for planting, like an onion set.

clue.text: Erased document about lease

indicators.note: the document goes round the lease

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
to let is to lease out property

explanation.surface: A lease agreement has been wiped from the files.
explanation.definitionFit: Removed or struck out, as text from a file.

clue.text: Mother, growing old, is hurtful

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
ageing, here spelt without the middle E

explanation.surface: A mother who is getting on in years makes cutting remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing harm or injury; detrimental.

clue.text: Plant person preceding Plymouth player

indicators.note: the person comes before the player in the answer

parts.note: a man is a person
Sir Francis Drake is said to have finished his game of bowls on Plymouth Hoe before facing the Armada

explanation.surface: Someone stands in front of a footballer from Plymouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plymouth player' suggests a footballer for Plymouth Argyle; it is Drake, the bowler on Plymouth Hoe in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean herb with a forked root, steeped in folklore.

clue.text: No employment for one on endless shift…

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letters shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on a never-ending shift has no real work to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work shift but is the anagram signal. The ellipsis joins this clue to 22 down, where 'shifts' returns as dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without work or occupation is a state of inactivity.

clue.text: Get an old coat, thanks to poet

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet is thanked with the gift of a vintage coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sleeveless tunic worn over armour by medieval knights or by heralds.

clue.text: … after strike-leader makes fun of shifts

indicators.note: the mocking comes after the first letter in the answer
the leader of the word is its first letter

parts.note: to mock is to make fun of

explanation.surface: Continuing 20 down: the union leader ridicules the workers' shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like work shifts but means loose dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a loose dress, and these are loose overgarments like it.

clue.text: Trial for freeloader

indicators.note: the letters are set free and loosed into another order

explanation.surface: A trial is held for a scrounger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freeloader' must be split: 'free' signals the anagram of LOADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or testing experience; historically a test by fire or water.

clue.text: I must have Gilbert and Sullivan overtures to talk about? That's a puzzle

indicators.note: the talk wraps round the other letters

parts.note: jaw is slang for talk or chatter

indicators.note: the overtures of the composers are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone insists on discussing the Savoy operas' overtures and finds it baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote the comic Savoy operas; their initials G and S follow I inside JAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces to be reassembled is a puzzle.

clue.text: Dancing bug

explanation.surface: Two words, perhaps for a stage show and a spy's gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of dancing with metal-plated shoes; also a listening device fitted to a phone line.

clue.text: Proposal for nurse

explanation.surface: A formal offer and a carer side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer or bid, as for a contract; also one who tends or looks after, like a nurse.

clue.text: A strict disciplinarian or an artist holds it right back

indicators.note: the artist's name keeps the other letters within it

parts.note: Edouard Manet was a French painter

indicators.note: the two words before it are read backwards together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stickler for rules or a painter who keeps something back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the run 'it right' round as a whole, giving RTI, which the French painter's name holds in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who demands rigid obedience to rules, after a severe French army drillmaster.

clue.text: Deal with name

explanation.surface: Coping with something and giving it a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or cope with; also a person's name or title, as in an online username.

clue.text: Trojan heroine finding salad plant on mountain

indicators.note: in an across answer, the plant comes first and the mountain follows it

parts.note: cress is a peppery salad plant
Mount Ida is a mountain near Troy

explanation.surface: A heroine from Troy comes upon greens growing on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: The faithless lover in Chaucer's and Shakespeare's tales of Troilus.

clue.text: Illusory sight of silver in mud

indicators.note: the silver sits inside the mud

parts.note: mire is boggy mud
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A glint of silver in a swamp turns out to be a trick of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion, such as water seen in a hot desert.

clue.text: Slim work translated by textile manufacturer

indicators.note: the letters are converted into another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A slim volume rendered into another language by a cloth maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'textile manufacturer' suggests a mill owner; it is the caterpillar that spins silk.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of a moth that spins a cocoon of fibre used to make silk.

clue.text: White herons, for example, having a rest break

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the letters break up and reform in a different order

explanation.surface: Wading birds take a rest from fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender white wading birds of the heron family.
